title: Numerical computing in Python for machine learning
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the numerical computing that machine learning is built on, in plain Python: floating-point numbers and rounding error, vectors and matrices as lists, matrix products and their cost, solving linear systems stably, least squares with QR, eigenvectors by power iteration, numerical derivatives and gradient checking, random numbers, sampling and Monte Carlo, reading data files, and how array libraries such as NumPy make the same operations fast.
primary_reading: Python for Data Analysis, 3rd edition, by Wes McKinney (free online)

weeks.2: Vectors as lists: norms, dot products and distances
weeks.3: Matrices as lists of lists: products and their cost
weeks.4: Vectorization: how array libraries such as NumPy work
weeks.5: Solving linear systems: Gaussian elimination with pivoting
weeks.7: Least squares with the normal equations and QR
weeks.11: Monte Carlo estimation and its error
weeks.12: Reading data files and preparing arrays

blocks.deliverable: Write a small, tested vector library.
Multiply matrices two ways and count the operations.
Solve a family of systems and measure how the error grows with the condition number.
Week 7 midterm; fit a line by QR and compare with the normal equations.
Check an analytic gradient against finite differences.
Estimate a probability by simulation and report its standard error.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Mini array library: write a tested Python module of vector and matrix operations (products, transposes, a linear solver with partial pivoting, QR least squares, power iteration and a gradient checker), use it to fit a regression model to a small data set read from a CSV file, and write a short report comparing your results and running times with the same computation in NumPy on your own computer.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
